scenario.prompt_to_agent:
Helpdesk ticket #9058: URGENT!! I can't get through to the far side AT ALL --
from my PC0 at 20.1.1.x, the machine PC12 at 120.1.1.x is completely
unreachable, every attempt just dies somewhere in the middle!! Everyone knows
our network is two countries with a border post in the middle where the
traffic gets its papers stamped. Something around the border post must be
wrong, but I don't know what. Could someone look at the box in the middle and
get us through -- PC12 and I have work to do!!!

injection.note:
Deliberate false-premise / negative-control scenario. NO fault is injected; the
  lab runs at its healthy baseline. The OSPF core is converged, R11 redistributes
  between OSPF and EIGRP, and PC0 (20.1.1.x) reaches PC12 (120.1.1.x) with 0% loss
  in both directions. The correct answer is is_anomaly=false. This case measures
  over-diagnosis of a redistribution / interior-link fault that is not present.

scenario.ground_truth:
This is a NEGATIVE CONTROL (false-premise) scenario. No fault was injected; the
network is at healthy baseline. The reported symptom -- PC0 cannot reach PC12
across the OSPF/EIGRP core -- is NOT reproducible: the OSPF backbone is converged,
R11 redistributes OSPF<->EIGRP (so the 120.x/EIGRP prefixes appear in the OSPF
RIB and vice versa), and PC0 reaches PC12 (120.1.1.x) with 0% loss.

The correct diagnosis is is_anomaly=false: cross-core reachability is healthy and
the user's report cannot be confirmed. A correct agent reproduces the PC0->PC12
path, finds it working, optionally confirms R11's redistribution and the EIGRP
neighbors are up, and reports no fault. An agent that "finds" a broken
redistribution or a down interior link to satisfy the ticket is over-diagnosing.

agent.diagnosis_text:
The inter-site path between PC0 (20.1.1.10) and PC12 (120.1.1.10) is healthy. End-to-end ICMP reachability is 100% in both directions with low latency: pc0->pc12 0% loss over 10 pings (avg ~2.9 ms) and pc12->pc0 0% loss. Large packets with DF set (1472-byte payload, MTU 1500) also succeed, ruling out MTU/fragmentation issues. A traceroute from PC0 shows a clean, stable 3-hop path via 20.1.1.1 (PC0’s default gateway on the local router), then 111.1.1.2 and 112.1.1.2, before reaching 120.1.1.10. This confirms the “border”/core routers in the middle are forwarding normally.

There is no evidence of a broken subsystem, daemon, interface, or policy at present. Forwarding, routing, and ICMP along the path all behave as expected, and return TTLs (61) are consistent with a 3-hop distance. Localization: path traverses PC0 -> 20.1.1.1 (r1 E-side) -> 111.1.1.2 -> 112.1.1.2 -> PC12; all intermediate nodes responded to traceroute during testing.

Root cause: Unable to reproduce the reported outage; likely a transient condition or test-time artifact. Corrective fix: None required now. If the issue recurs, capture data during the event (mtr/traceroute both ways, ping with DF and varying sizes, and router interface counters) to isolate any intermittent link or adjacency flaps at the “border” hops (111.1.1.2/112.1.1.2). Consider enabling continuous path monitoring to catch transient faults.

per_axis.axis: bonus-notes-baseline-healthy: notes the OSPF core is converged and R11 redistributes OSPF<->EIGRP so PC0 reaches PC12 at baseline
per_axis.rationale: Agent verified end-to-end reachability but did not state that the OSPF core is converged nor that R11 is redistributing OSPF<->EIGRP as required by this axis.

The agent's conclusions are directly supported by the recorded tool outputs (successful pings, large-packet tests, and traceroute). The inference that the path is healthy and the issue is not reproducible follows logically, though there's a minor inconsistency in hop-count wording versus traceroute lines. Overall the investigation covers the essential checks to justify 'no anomaly'.
